ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Initially, 0.10 mole of solid manna is heated at a constant rate at room temperature, and heating is continued until it completely boils. Assume the manna gas is an ideal gas. The described phase change is: $$\text{ga(l)} \rightarrow \text{ga(g)}$$ The standard enthalpy changes $h^\circ$ of the substances (unit: $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) are: - $\text{ga(l)}$: $5.60$ - $\text{ga(g)}$: $277.1$ It is known that the enthalpy of vaporization of manna is $271.5\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, and the $\Delta S^\circ = 113.4\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\ \text{K}^{-1}$ of this boiling process. Find the boiling-point temperature of manna (unit: K).

raw_record.question_text:
Initially, 0.10 mole of solid manna is heated at a constant rate at room temperature, and heating is continued until it completely boils. Assume the manna gas is an ideal gas. The described phase change is:

$$\text{ga(l)} \rightarrow \text{ga(g)}$$

The standard enthalpy changes $h^\circ$ of the substances (unit: $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) are:
- $\text{ga(l)}$: $5.60$
- $\text{ga(g)}$: $277.1$

It is known that the enthalpy of vaporization of manna is $271.5\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, and the $\Delta S^\circ = 113.4\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\ \text{K}^{-1}$ of this boiling process. Find the boiling-point temperature of manna (unit: K).

method.method_draft: Describe the image as a heating curve with a temperature plateau, confirming that a phase change occurs under continued heating. From the text, take ΔH_vap = 271.5 kJ mol^-1 and ΔS° = 113.4 J mol^-1 K^-1 for ga(l) → ga(g). Convert ΔH_vap to 271500 J mol^-1. Apply the boiling-equilibrium condition ΔG = 0 = ΔH - TΔS, so T_b = 271500 / 113.4 K, giving approximately 2394 K.

claims.claim: The phase change given in the problem is ga(l) → ga(g).
claims.label: perception
claims.source: The phase change given in the problem is ga(l) → ga(g)

claims.claim: ga(l) → ga(g) corresponds to the boiling/vaporization process.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The enthalpy of vaporization of this process can be calculated from h°[ga(g)] - h°[ga(l)].
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The value of h°[ga(g)] is 277.1 kJ mol^-1.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The value of h°[ga(l)] is 5.60 kJ mol^-1.
claims.label: perception

claims.claim: The calculated 271.5 kJ mol^-1 is consistent with the enthalpy of vaporization in the problem.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Is consistent with the enthalpy of vaporization in the problem

claims.claim: 271.5 kJ mol^-1 converted to SI units is 271500 J mol^-1.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: At the boiling point, when liquid-gas equilibrium occurs, ΔG = 0.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: At the boiling point, liquid-gas equilibrium occurs, ΔG = 0

claims.claim: The Gibbs free energy relation is ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.
claims.label: knowledge

claims.claim: From 0 = ΔH - TΔS, T_b = ΔH/ΔS can be obtained.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: Substituting the numerical values gives T_b = 271500 / 113.4 K.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The boiling-point temperature rounded to an integer is approximately 2394 K.
claims.label: reasoning
